result.title: A chess world champion explains what the game can teach us about life
result.description:
'Sometimes the best move does not equal a perfect outcome. Sometimes there are no best moves, but the one that suits you the most.’

At 14, Yifan Hou became a #chess grandmaster. At 16, she became the youngest ever Women’s World Chess Champion - a record she holds to this day. Here, she explains how the game has shaped her worldview, and what it has taught her about taking on life’s challenges. 

Yifan Hou is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader.

result.title: AI debt, hedge-fund power and Africa's new credit ratings agency
result.description:
How worried are investors about AI-related debt?

In our latest roundup of finance and economic news:

- The AI boom has a growing debt problem, despite making up nearly two-thirds of US venture-capital investment over the past year.
- Hedge funds are expanding their footprint in financial markets, with assets under management now triple what they were in 2013.
- #Africa launches its own credit rating agency (#AfCRA) to offer an alternative perspective on the continent’s economies. 

World Economic Forum digital editor Spencer Feingold breaks down the latest developments being tracked by the organisation's Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems. 

You can read the full round-up for the latest finance stories: https://www.weforum.org/stories/financial-and-monetary-systems/chief-economists-on-debt-yields-ai-and-other-finance-news-to-know

result.title: Turbines Built For Typhoons & Should We Trust AI Agents? | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - Should we trust AI agents?:
Three experts discuss: Omar Sultan Al Olama, Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence for the United Arab Emirates; Mark-Alexandre Doumba, Minister of Digital Economy and Innovation for Gabon; and Yalda Aoukar, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Bracket Capital.

04.18 - Top 5 global economic challenges:
The high cost of living, rising debt levels and teething problems in AI are just some of the thorny issues facing the global economy identified in the IMF’s October 2026 World Economic Outlook. Here, we compare the findings with our own latest Chief Economists’ Outlook, which surveys leading experts to identify challenges and opportunities in the year ahead.

06.23 - Turbines built for typhoons:
Wind turbines are a key part of the energy transition, but they remain vulnerable to hurricane-force winds, which can snap their blades and buckle their towers. Ming Yang Smart Energy Group has designed Ocean X, a lighter, twin-rotor model that has already withstood a once-in-a-generation typhoon.

result.title: Ideas On The Move: Mina Guli
result.description:
‘Water is everything, but for too long we’ve treated it as if it were nothing.’

Water advocate @MinaGuliWater didn’t set out to be an ultra-runner, something she says she’s neither good at nor enjoys. But after seeing South Africa's Orange River at a historic low, she knew she had to act. 

Since then she has run 200 marathons in a year, started the Thirst Foundation and helped build a global movement that has reached people in more than 200 countries and territories. 

She joined us at #AMGFL26 in Dubai to explain why water is an issue we can’t afford to ignore.
